newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-PEN PICTURES OF BARCELONA PLAYERS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PEN PICTURES OF BARCELONA PLAYERS.

text.p: Pen pictures of Barcelona players ahead of Wednesday's European Cup Winners' Cup final against Paris St Germain in Rotterdam:
Vitor Baia. Goalkeeper. Age 27. The Portuguese international keeper signed from Porto in the close season for $6.34 million. After a good start to his Barcelona career, he has recently looked shaky.
Carlos Busquets. Goalkeeper. 29. Nearly ever-present last season, Busquets has failed to impress in his few chances since the arrival of Baia.

Albert Ferrer. Defender. 26. Right-sided defender who won a gold medal with Spain at the 1992 Olympics. Ferrer makes up for a lack of physical presence with a terrier-like determination down the touchline but has struggled to secure a first team place under Robson.

Abelardo Fernandez. Defender. 27. An experienced Spanish international, Abelardo is sometimes sidelined because of the wealth of central defenders in the Barcelona line-up. Dangerous in the air, particularly at set-pieces.
Laurent Blanc. Defender. 31. The Frenchman was one of Johan Cruyff's last signings and has quietly made himself an important element at the centre of Bobby Robson's defence.
Fernando Couto. Defender. 27. One of three Portuguese internationals in the Barcelona squad, Couto has struggled to find a place in central defence.
Sergi Barjuan. Defender. 24. A key factor down the left in both defence and attack, Sergi is one of the quickest men in the Spanish game and an instant first choice.
Miguel Angel Nadal. Defender/midfielder. 30. Surprisingly skillful for a big man, Nadal's strength can make him a match-winner in the air at set-pieces.
Gheorghe Popescu. Defender/midfielder. 29. Former Spurs' man who sometimes captains the side. Strong coming forward, Popescu is also a set-piece specialist and occasional penalty-taker.

Luis Enrique Martinez. Defender/midfielder. 26 (27 on Thursday). Energetic utility player who pops up in virtually every position and has blossomed since signing from Real Madrid in the close-season, scoring a surprising 15 goals.
Josep Guardiola. Midfielder. 26. Classy and intelligent, Guardiola has returned to favour under Robson after being sidelined by Cruyff and now regularly captains the team. Crafty free-kick man.

Ivan de la Pena. Midfielder. 21. The shaven-headed darling of the Camp Nou crowd is one of the best passers and set-piece men in the Spanish game. The inconsistent De la Pena, who turned 21 on Tuesday, is back in favour after being sidelined.
Guillermo Amor. Midfielder. 29. Came good at the end of last season with a series of crucial goals which earned him a Euro 96 slot, but has hardly played under Robson.
Roger Garcia. Midfielder. 19. A regular under Cruyff, Roger has found himself ousted by the arrival of foreign stars.

Giovanni. Midfielder/striker. 25. Traded Pele's number 10 shirt at Santos for the playmaker role at Barcelona. A fine finisher and a particularly good header of the ball, Giovanni is the ideal foil to compatriot Ronaldo. Has clashed with Robson after being dropped on several occasions. Carried off injured in the 1-0 win over Real Madrid on Saturday.
Luis Figo. Striker. 24. Skilful Portuguese international who is at home down either the left or right wing. Recently linked with a move to AC Milan.

Ronaldo. Striker. 20. A series of sensational individual goals has made Ronaldo the undisputed king of the Spanish game and has already gone a long way to justifying the then world record $20 million paid to PSV Eindhoven in the close season. Scored the only goal against Real Madrid on Saturday.

Juan Pizzi. Striker. 28. A naturalized Argentine who was Spain's top goalscorer while at Tenerife last season, Pizzi has been left in the shadow of Ronaldo since joining Barcelona. Reputation for squandering easy chances.

Hristo Stoichkov. Striker. 31. Fiery Bulgarian international who has recovered his form after a bad start to his second spell at Barcelona since returning from an unsuccessful season at Italy's Parma.

Emmanuel Amunike. Striker. 26. Robson's only mid-season signing, the Nigerian international winger has not found his touch down the left side of the attack, and is frequently the subject of whistling from an anti-Robson section of the Camp Nou crowd.
